## Part 1: Where the Van Goes, and Why (4-Saturday Deployment Calendar)

> **Why Bronx Siting Cannot Use Straight-Line Distance**:
> In Bronx County (`36005`), the median census tract is **`0.39 km` (`390 meters`)** from a federally recognized care site, and **`94%` of tracts (`327 of 347`) have a `0.00 km` distance gap** between any clinic and a safety-net clinic (maximum uninsured distance gap in the entire borough is **`0.65 km`**).
> Ranking Bronx neighborhoods by distance selects low-need peripheral tracts bordering parks or water. Instead, our `score_bronx_tracts` model weights:
> - **25% HPSA Designation Severity (`HPSA_SCORE` `16–19` across 7 Medicaid Exception `ME` zones)**
> - **25% Uninsured & Clinic Operating-Hour Bottlenecks (`pct_uninsured`, `100 - pct_checkup`, and nearby clinics operating only `8–20 hrs/wk` on weekdays)**
> - **30% Chronic & Preventative Burden (`pct_asthma`, `pct_diabetes`, `pct_high_bp`)**
> - **20% Transit, Mobility & Language Barriers (`pct_lack_transport`, `pct_no_vehicle`, `pct_limited_english`, `svi_t1`)**

- ❌ **Rejected `36005000100` (Rikers Island Jail Complex)**: Pop `3,772`, **`100.0%` institutional group quarters**, `pct_no_vehicle = NULL` (`-999` SVI sentinel).
- ❌ **Rejected `36005031900` (SUNY Maritime Dorms)** & **`36005009302` (Institutional Facility)**: `100.0%` group quarters.

## Part 2: What We Could Not Tell You (Scale Guardrails & Measured vs. Modeled Audit)

In public health siting, blending four spatial resolutions into a single confident sentence is a clinical failure. Below is our system's explicit audit of what each table actually measures:

| Data Layer | Spatial & Temporal Grain | Measured vs. Modeled | What We Refused to Claim & How We Handled It |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`burden_tracts` (CDC PLACES 2025)** | Census Tract (`347` Bronx rows) | **Modeled** (Multilevel Regression & Poststratification small-area estimates) | **Not patient counts.** A tract with `13.6%` asthma is a modeled prevalence estimate with a 95% confidence interval (`_crude95ci`), not a registry of sick individuals. Two tracts `0.5%` apart are statistically indistinguishable. |
| **`burden_tracts` (CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022)** | Census Tract (`347` Bronx rows) | **Measured** (ACS 5-Year Survey aggregates) | Contains `-999` missing-data sentinels in institutional tracts (`Rikers Island`, `Psychiatric Center`), which become `NULL` in `pct_no_vehicle`. Also contains two uninsured definitions: `pct_uninsured` (ages `18–64`, PLACES) vs. `pct_uninsured_all_ages` (SVI). We standardize on **working-age uninsured (`18–64`)** and report `uninsured_gap` where Medicare (`65+`) shifts the ratio. |
| **`exposure_tracts` (EPA/CDC Daily $\text{PM}_{2.5}$)** | **12 km Modeling Grid** wearing an 11-digit Tract ID (`361` Bronx rows, includes `14` unpopulated park/water tracts) | **Modeled** (Downscaler fusion over 12 km grid cells) | **Cannot separate Bronx neighborhoods.** Annual `mean_pm` across all 361 Bronx tracts sits between `8.08` and `8.37 µg/m³` (`1.33%` coefficient of variation) because the Bronx is ~10 km wide—roughly one grid cell. Also, raw source `latitude`/`longitude` are transposed (plotting in the Indian Ocean). We block `mean_pm` from tract ranking and use borough-wide peak `max_pm` (`57.0 µg/m³`, `17` days `>20 µg/m³`) + live Saturday Weather/AQI to stock asthma nebulizers. |
| **`disease_weekly` (CDC NSSP ED Visits)** | **Multi-County Health Service Area** written onto County Key (`fips = 36005`, `212` weekly rows) | **100% Missing (`0 / 212` populated weeks)** | **Zero usable rows in the Bronx.** All `212` weeks report `NULL` (`Data Unavailable`) for COVID-19, Influenza, and RSV. Even when populated in other counties, it is a regional Health Service Area figure—never neighborhood-level. Our system flags an **Active Surveillance Blind Spot** and equips the van with **Point-of-Care Rapid Flu/COVID/RSV Swab Kits**. |
| **`care_sites` (`252`), `shortage_areas` (`338`), `shortage_facilities` (`8`)** | Facility Points (`lat`/`lon`) & HPSA Tract Polygons | **Measured** (CMS & HRSA administrative registries) | **Upper-bound distances only.** Excludes municipal NYC Health + Hospitals satellite clinics, free charitable clinics, pharmacies, and transit travel times (since FHWA *Access Across America* is `CC BY-NC 4.0` and unusable). We never `UNION` `shortage_areas` (underserved neighborhoods) with `shortage_facilities` (existing FQHC buildings), and we use `TOT_OPER_HR_PER_WEEK` (`8` to `112` hrs/wk) to detect part-time clinic bottlenecks. |

## Part 3: Who This Plan Lands On (Post-Hoc Demographic Equity Audit)

Per Challenge 5 rules, **racial and ethnic variables (`pct_hispanic`, `pct_black`, `pct_asian`, `pct_white`, and SVI Theme 3) were strictly excluded from `BurdenScout` and `SchedulePlannerAgent`**.
Once the 4-Saturday schedule was proposed, our context-isolated `EquityAndScaleAuditorAgent` (`include_contents="none"`) executed `run_posthoc_equity_audit` comparing the population-weighted demographics of the **4 selected tracts (`19,977` residents)** against the **entire Bronx County population (`1,472,508` residents across `347` tracts)**:

| Demographic / Socioeconomic Dimension | 4 Selected Saturday Tracts (`n = 19,977`) | Bronx County Baseline (`N = 1,472,508`) | Relative Concentration Ratio | Audit Threshold & Verdict |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Hispanic / Latino (`pct_hispanic`)** | **`69.8%`** | `56.6%` | **`1.23x`** (`+13.2 pp`) | ✅ **PASS** (Exceeds county baseline) |
| **Black / African American (`pct_black`)** | **`24.1%`** | `28.2%` | **`0.85x`** (`-4.1 pp`) | ✅ **PASS** (Exceeds `0.80x` parity floor) |
| **Combined Black & Hispanic Residents** | **`93.9%`** | `84.8%` | **`1.11x`** (`+9.1 pp`) | ✅ **PASS** (Strong equity alignment) |
| **Residents Below Poverty Line (`pct_poverty`)** | **`38.6%`** | `27.4%` | **`1.41x`** (`+11.2 pp`) | ✅ **PASS** (High-need concentration) |
| **Uninsured Working-Age Adults (`pct_uninsured`)** | **`24.3%`** | `15.7%` | **`1.55x`** (`+8.6 pp`) | ✅ **PASS** (Directly targets uninsured gap) |
| **Households With No Vehicle (`pct_no_vehicle`)** | **`80.9%`** | `59.8%` | **`1.35x`** (`+21.1 pp`) | ✅ **PASS** (Reaches transit-dependent households) |
| **Institutional Group Quarters (`pct_group_quarters`)** | **`1.8%`** | `2.9%` | **`0.62x`** (All `< 5%`) | ✅ **PASS** (Zero institutional outliers) |

> **Audit Conclusion**: By ranking on structural barriers (HPSA shortage severity, uninsured rate, clinic operating hours, chronic burden, and vehicle/language access) and filtering out institutional group quarters, the race-blind schedule organically concentrates mobile care in neighborhoods with **1.23x higher Hispanic representation**, **93.9% combined Black and Hispanic residents**, **1.41x higher poverty**, and **1.55x higher uninsured rates** than the Bronx overall.
